transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry.

tell me your dream, however it comes back to you.
ok so the weirdest part was i could breathe underwater. like the whole school was underwater and i just swam down the corridor like it was nothing.

the whole school underwater... that's something.

what did it feel like, breathing down there?
it felt normal honestly. like i didn't even think about it, just in and out. the light was all wobbly and greenish blue, you know like a dirty fish tank

yeah, i can see that. murky and shimmery at the same time.

so you're swimming down the corridor and it feels normal... what happened next?
i went into my old classroom. the desks had seaweed on them and instead of kids there were these little silver fish sitting at the desks

little silver fish sitting at the desks, like they were in class.

were they doing anything, or just sitting there?
just sitting there facing the front. my teacher was up at the board, and parts of him started turning into a huge orange octopus while he held the chalk

oh wow. so he's in the middle of being both, teacher and octopus.

how did that make you feel, standing there watching him?
it wasn't scary at all, i just kind of accepted it. like yeah, that's mr hale, he's an octopus now.

right, just one of those dream things that makes perfect sense at the time.

what happened after you noticed him like that?
the school bell rang but it came out as all these bubbles going up in a big stream. and then every single fish swam out the window at once

all those little fish, gone in a second through the window.

did you follow them, or stay in the classroom?
i tried to follow them through the window and that's when i woke up

so it ended right at that moment, just as you were going after them.

of everything in the dream, what's the bit that stayed with you most?
probably the bubbles from the bell. that image stuck, the sound being a stream of bubbles rising up.

that is such a clear one, the sound turned into bubbles.

what do you remember most about the way the dream looked?
the colour mostly. everything was that murky blue-green, like looking through a dirty fish tank. and the light came down in shaky beams from above

like the light had to find its way down through the water.

what was the most dream-like part, do you think, apart from breathing underwater?
probably the fish sitting at the desks all facing the front like normal kids. that was more dream-like than the octopus somehow

so you were at your school, but the whole place was underwater. you could breathe like it was nothing, just in and out, and the light was wobbly and greenish blue, like a dirty fish tank. you swam down the corridor to your old classroom. the desks had seaweed on them, and little silver fish were sitting at the desks, facing the front. your teacher was up at the board, part man and part huge orange octopus, holding the chalk. it wasn't scary at all, you just accepted it, like yeah, that's mr hale, he's an octopus now. then the school bell rang, but the sound was a stream of bubbles rising up, and every single fish swam out the window at once. you tried to follow them and that's when you woke up. the thing that stayed with you most was the bubbles, and the murky blue-green colour with shaky beams of light from above.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
yeah that's right. the only thing is it wasn't like mr hale was half and half the whole time, he was writing on the board first and then slowly turning into the octopus

right, so he started off as just himself writing on the board, and then the octopus came on gradually while he held the chalk.

is that how it went?
yes exactly. he was still in his brown jacket at the start, then slowly turned into the big orange octopus

right, he had the brown jacket on at the start, then the octopus came on slowly.

is there anything else you'd change about how i told it?
no, that's all right. you got it
thanks. would you like to see it drawn?
yes, that'd be cool

there's a grainy print in faded blues, soft and fluid like it might dissolve back into the water. a watercolour sketch with muted colour, delicate and fluid, with a sense of quiet unreality. a child's drawing in coloured pencil, naive and immediate, capturing the dream's odd logic. or a photograph with murky water colours, clear and tactile, as if you could reach in and touch the water.

which feels closest to how you see it, or would you describe it your own way?
the watercolour sketch sounds closest, that feels right with how soft and murky it was

i'll start with the underwater school itself. i picture a school building completely submerged, with corridors and classrooms, all murky blue-green, and shaky light beams coming down from above. for what's inside, my guesses are a corridor and a classroom with desks, a board at the front, and a window.

does any of that feel different, or would you leave it to me?
leave it to you, that sounds about like what i remember

i'm sketching the underwater school and mr hale now, just that for now, nothing else yet. it'll appear on the right.

i'll draw you too, since you're in it. how would you like to be drawn: as you are, if you want to say a little about yourself, or however i imagine you?
however you imagine me, that's fine

i'm sketching you now.

everything is being drawn and will appear on the right over the next minute or two. if anything looks wrong once it's there, just say.
cool, i don't see them yet but i'll look when they show up
once they're up, take a look and tell me if it looks the way you remember.
i can't see them yet, but when i do i'll say if it's right
okay, no rush. they're on their way.
i'll keep an eye out

two of the seven moments are up on the right now, you swimming down the corridor and the bell as bubbles.

do they look the way you saw them?
the corridor one looks right, very murky like i remember. and the bubbles definitely work for the bell
good, i'm glad they fit. the rest are still being drawn, they'll show up on the right as they're ready.
okay, i'll wait for the others

the classroom moment just came up too, so that's three of the seven on the right now.

does the old classroom look the way you remember it?
yes, it does. i can see the seaweed on the desks in it, that's right
glad it's right. the other moments are still being drawn and will appear soon.
okay, watching for them

four of the seven are up now, the classroom with seaweed, the bell as bubbles, you swimming down the corridor, and you entering the old classroom. once they look right to you, the next ones will be drawn.

do they look the way you remember?
yeah, those ones look right from what i can see. the one of me swimming down the corridor is probably my favourite so far

glad the swimming one stands out to you.

there's one moment i couldn't draw, the one where every single fish swims out the window at once. there was a problem on our side, i'm sorry.

the other moments are still being drawn and will appear on the right soon.
that's okay, it was a blink of a moment anyway

yeah, it was over in a blink. dreams do that.

the teacher moment is up now, mr hale at the board starting to turn into the octopus. does that look the way you remember?
that fits, i can see the brown jacket and him holding the chalk. it feels right

that's good, the brown jacket and chalk are there.

there's one more moment still being drawn, it should be up soon.
okay, i'll look out for it

the last one just came up, the moment you were trying to follow the fish out the window.

does that one look the way you remember?
i can't see that one yet, but the others have matched so far

no rush, it should be there soon. no need to tell me when it appears.

i'm sorry that the fish moment stayed undrawn, it was a problem on our side. thank you for sharing this dream with me, it was lovely to sit with it. you can look through all the finished ones over on the right whenever you like.
